headline: Cornered Afghan Foes Hope Winter Will Slow the Taliban
snippet: Afghanistan's Taliban militia, largely unstoppable since start of its nationwide march in 1995, adds more territory to domain during summer, winning victories in country's northeast, including capture of strategically important city of Taliqan in September after 33-day battle; currently controls estimated 90 to 95 percent of country that has been at war for 21 years, leaving smidgen to government of Pres Burhanuddin Rabbani, considered legimimate by most of world; Ahmad Shah Massoud, Rabbani's military commander, is desperately trying to hold his army together to launch counteroffensive; is optimistic winter's deep snows and punishing winds will slow Taliban's advance and lead to recapture of city, which is on major supply route; map; photo (M)
